extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, university administrators, and the academic research community
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and considerations used (and contested) when a university decides to downsize or eliminate graduate programs in a department, illustrated by the University of Rochester case. Includes metrics used by administrators and the counter-arguments offered by faculty and outside reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality of the discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the discipline is 'central' to the university's other programs and mission (the administration looked at 'centrality of the discipline' when deciding which graduate programs to cut).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration asked other departments whether the Mathematics Department was central to their programs; if many departments report 'math is not central', that was treated as justification for cuts. Counterargument: abstract intellectual centrality may differ from practical perceptions; centrality can be manifested through specialized strengths that are highly relevant to some fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkages and interactions with other departments
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree and character of interactions (joint research, shared courses, institutionalized programs) between the department and other departments on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration relied on interviews with faculty across departments and concluded interactions were 'very few' and often ad hoc (single projects or courses) rather than institutionalized. The department presented examples of joint research and cross-attendance in graduate classes. Guidance/anti-pattern: robust, institutionalized linkages score better than sporadic, ad-hoc collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of undergraduate instruction (especially calculus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception and evidence regarding whether undergraduate instruction provided by the department is 'optimal'—with particular focus on calculus teaching for large numbers of students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration cited anecdotal reports from tutoring centers and faculty dissatisfaction with calculus. The department countered with student evaluations showing comparable or higher satisfaction and noted attempts to address issues (task force, meetings). Scoring should consider objective data (evaluations, tutoring metrics) and whether remedial steps have been taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department initiative to address instructional problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the department has taken proactive steps to address perceived or actual undergraduate teaching issues (e.g., forming task forces, coordinating courses, developing tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aslin: 'What you look for is initiative on the part of the department.. to begin to address' nationwide/local concerns. Examples include task forces on calculus, meetings with science departments, coordinated course arrangements, development of computer homework feedback tools. Lack of initiative was used against the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on external rankings (NRC, U.S. News) as evidentiary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of published rankings (National Research Council, U.S. News & World Report) as a primary source of external information about program quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administration relied heavily on NRC and U.S. News rankings; this was criticized because rankings may be based on hearsay/intuition and underrate departments with specialized strengths. Guidance: treat rankings as one input, not sole decisive evidence; be cautious about disciplinary/subfield distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external site visits / outside evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing in outside, discipline-respected site-visit teams to evaluate a department as an alternative to relying solely on rankings or internal interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics recommended external evaluations as they provide 'very good information' if parameters and reviewers are set properly. Administration argued outside review of targeted programs might be biased. Guidance: well-constructed external reviews can contextualize role and contributions of a department and reveal subfield strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty size relative to institutional teaching needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the department's faculty numbers are necessary to staff required teaching (especially lab- or large-enrollment courses) across the university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators avoided cutting biology/chemistry partly because their faculty numbers were critical to staff lab-based courses for many pre-med students. For mathematics, the administration felt graduate students and tenure-track faculty were not the only means of delivering undergraduate calculus. Guidance: evaluate staffing implications for cross-departmental curricular obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research productivity and external support
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of research activity and success at attracting external funding (grants), and the dollar magnitude relative to other disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mathematics Department had many faculty with grants (nearly two thirds), but total dollar amounts were smaller than in other disciplines. Guidance: consider both number of active researchers and funding scale; specialized excellence may not translate to large dollar totals but can be high impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of graduate students for disciplinary research
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether graduate students are imperative to carrying out high-quality research in that discipline (administration argued grad students were not imperative in mathematics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jackson: 'you can do a lot of distinguished research without the Ph.D. program.' Opposing view: many argue graduate programs are central to sustaining research, cross-fertilization, and advanced course offerings. Evaluation should consider discipline-specific norms for graduate student involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to attract and retain high-quality faculty and students
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether eliminating or reducing a graduate program will harm the university's attractiveness to prospective undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty—and thereby damage long-term reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protesters argued that without a graduate program Rochester would be less attractive to students and top faculty, harming recruitment and the 'intellectual tone' of the university. Guidance: assess downstream effects on recruitment and reputation when considering program cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of specialized subfield strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounting for departments' specialized areas of excellence that may not be captured by broad rankings (e.g., algebraic topology excellence at Rochester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics noted that rankings underrate departments with specialized strengths; Freedman: 'departments with specialized strength will be underrated.' Guidance: evaluations should identify subfield excellence and downstream impacts on related disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, dialogue, and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: The fairness and openness of the decision-making process, including whether affected departments had meaningful chances to respond to data and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints that administration 'held its cards close' and 'never gave them a chance to respond.' Lowengrub: lack of dialogue is a serious flaw. Guidance: include department input, allow rebuttal, and provide transparent criteria and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of political rather than academic decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether cuts are driven by political considerations (spreading cuts, desired targets) rather than strictly academic or mission-based criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers suggested politics influenced spread of cuts across fields; 'some of the rhetoric was clearly such that they knew what they wanted to prove and then went back and got the information they needed.' Guidance: guard evaluations against confirmation bias and political objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching model and use of adjuncts versus tenure-track faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of proposals to cover lower-level or large-enrollment courses with adjuncts or nonresearch faculty and the expected impact on instruction quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics warned adjunct-based instruction is 'typically cheap, and you get what you pay for' and predicted a 'significant lowering of the quality of instruction.' Guidance: weigh cost savings against likely declines in teaching quality and student experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local industry and disciplinary ecosystem needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the department's role in supporting local industry and the broader regional research ecosystem (e.g., optics and imaging companies near Rochester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry voices (Kodak, Xerox) argued elimination of math graduate research would harm imaging research and the companies' ability to recruit talent. Guidance: include local economic/industry impacts when evaluating the broader consequences of program changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial necessity and target savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether eliminating or reducing a program is justified by concrete budgetary targets and how that choice compares to alternatives for achieving savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration framed cuts as needed to address severe financial issues (e.g., 20% student, 10% faculty reductions). Critics countered that choices of which programs to cut should consider mission and alternative solutions; selection perceived as driven by which cuts would achieve required dollar amounts.
